clue.text: Horse box used by enthusiast

blocks.note: a chest is a large box or trunk
a nut is a fan, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A horsebox being driven around by some keen rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse box' reads as one object, but the horse is the definition and the box starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a horse with a reddish-brown coat, so the colour name stands for the animal.

clue.text: Lady’s weary catching fourth rabbit perhaps

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece closes round the other

blocks.note: her is the possessive for a woman
to bore someone is to weary them
IV is the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A woman is tired out from chasing a fourth rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit eats only plants, so it is an example of a plant-eating animal.

clue.text: Most important woman maintains casing of paper printing unit

indicators.note: a casing is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept
to maintain is to hold, so one piece holds the others inside

blocks.note: Sue is a woman's name
the first and last letters of paper
an em is a unit of measure in printing

explanation.surface: The chief woman in charge of a print works looks after its paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or greatest, so it describes whatever matters most.

clue.text: Food from 18’s house accompanied by uplifting drink

indicators.note: in a down entry uplifting raises the word, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a can of beer, so a drink
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A dish from a Mexican home served with a cheering drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-across is MEXICO. The ’s stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip baked with cheese, a snack of Mexican origin.

clue.text: Marathon character would be in shade when training finishes

indicators.note: the training finishes the longer word, so taking it off the end leaves what is wanted

blocks.note: taupe is a brownish-grey shade
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: A marathon runner is resting in the shade after training ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon is a town in Greece, so its characters are Greek letters, not runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the kind of character written in Marathon.

clue.text: Cut round end of flap and join together

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
going round something means wrapping it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to slice is to cut
the last letter of flap

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming the end of a flap of material and fixing it to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice is to join two ends, as of rope or film, by interweaving or overlapping them.

clue.text: Celestial body in the East shining? The opposite

blocks.note: Saturn is a planet
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A planet glittering in the eastern sky, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'The opposite' turn shining round: the definition is the reverse of bright and sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and sullen in temperament, the reverse of a sunny or shining disposition.

clue.text: 7 9’s teammate falls on part of head causing complaint

blocks.note: 9-across is a prop, and a lock is another forward in the same rugby scrum
the jaw is part of the head

explanation.surface: A rugby player lands on someone's head and is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 at the start is a stray from the book's text: only 9-across's teammate is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is tetanus, a disease, and complaint is a general word for an illness.

clue.text: Group regulars going through cold turkey

indicators.note: something going through another passes into its middle, so one piece ends up inside

blocks.note: UNPARSED: no standard sense of this word gives this letter; the book text may be misread
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a turkey is slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A support group of regulars helping one another quit something abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: Warning: this parse is incomplete. C and ASS are sound, but nothing in 'regulars' gives the L, so the answer rests on the definition and the crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a set of people or things grouped by shared qualities, a synonym of group.

clue.text: One trained at front of pack

definitions.text: One trained at front of pack

blocks.clueFragment: One trained at front of pack
blocks.note: surface reading: a trained dog or athlete leading the field
setter's reading: a rugby forward packing down in the front row of the scrum, the scrum being called the pack

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the forwards are called the pack, and the two players either side of the hooker in its front row have this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop forward is a drilled player who binds at the front of a rugby scrum, so the clue describes one.

clue.text: Lobster perhaps reddish? Serve in container

indicators.note: putting something in a vessel means it sits inside, enclosed by it

blocks.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
in tennis an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether the lobster looks red enough to be served in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' looks like a cooking instruction, but it is a tennis term here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobsters are an example of the class of hard-shelled sea creatures that includes crabs and shrimps.

clue.text: Submarine worker eats dessert in military craft

indicators.note: what someone eats goes inside them, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a diver works under the water
a bombe is a frozen dessert made in a dome-shaped mould

explanation.surface: A navy diver tucks into a pudding aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submarine' looks like the vessel, but it is an adjective meaning underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive bomber is a warplane that drops its bombs while plunging steeply at the target, so it is an aircraft of war.

clue.text: Young female smoker discussed illness

indicators.note: something discussed is talked about, so the word counts by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: bird is British slang for a young woman
a flue is a chimney duct that carries smoke away

explanation.surface: People talking about a girl who smokes and has fallen ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' looks like a person with a cigarette, but it is a chimney pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird flu is avian influenza, a disease that can pass from poultry to people.

clue.text: Only modify, removing plug

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so those letters drop out of the longer word

blocks.note: to adjust is to modify slightly
a plug is a piece of promotion, an advert

explanation.surface: Advice to make only a small change, such as taking out a stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' suggests a bung or a socket, but it means a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms as adverbs meaning merely, as in only a child or just a child.

clue.text: Landlord’s comparatively virtuous about time for vacating

indicators.note: vacating a place leaves it empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters
about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

blocks.note: holier is the comparative of holy
the first and last letters of time

explanation.surface: A landlord claims to be more upright than others about when tenants must leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for is. HOLIER splits after HO to take TE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier keeps a hotel, and the British sense of landlord covers someone who runs a pub or inn.

clue.text: Club team is one showing great fortitude

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club
a side is a team
is shortens to 's

explanation.surface: A sports club's team proves very brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club team' reads as one phrase, but the club is in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironsides is a person of great courage and endurance, the nickname given to Oliver Cromwell.

clue.text: Private accepted hostilities abroad ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is wanted

blocks.note: in means accepted or fashionable, as in the in crowd
war is open hostilities
the last letter of abroad

explanation.surface: A soldier took part in fighting overseas in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning personal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inward feelings are private ones, held within and not shown to others.

clue.text: Began swimming in small stream — sound familiar?

indicators.note: swimming letters move about, so they settle in a new order
in places the rearranged letters inside the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a rill is a tiny brook

explanation.surface: Someone started swimming in a brook and asks whether this is familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rings a bell seems familiar, an idiom for prompting a memory.

clue.text: Country doctor covering no longer in charge

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping round it, so one piece goes outside the others

blocks.note: MO is medical officer, an army doctor
ex means former, no longer what one was
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A rural GP standing in for someone who has retired from running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' reads as one phrase, but the country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation of North America, an example of a country.

clue.text: Send up soldier with common sense to keep close to line of fire

indicators.note: in a down entry sending something up raises it, so it reads bottom to top
the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
nous is practical intelligence
the last letter of line

explanation.surface: Mock a sensible soldier for staying near the line of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line of fire' reads as a phrase, but it splits: the line gives a letter and 'of fire' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous means relating to fire, and is used of rocks formed from molten material.

clue.text: Regularly visit pack member with failing heart, in distress

indicators.note: a failing heart gives out, so the middle letter is lost
in puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a queen is one of the cards in a pack
to fret is to be distressed and anxious

explanation.surface: Someone keeps calling on an ailing member of a group, worried sick.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEEN has two middle letters, both E; one goes. 'Pack member' suggests a wolf or a Scout, but the pack is of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there often, a verb synonym of visiting regularly.

clue.text: How IT set becomes upset in game?

blocks.note: to turn the words IT set into upset, a two-letter word of direction must take the place of the IT

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a computing team got rattled during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the instruction itself: put UP in place of IT, and IT SET becomes UPSET.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means willing and ready to try something, just like being keen on it.

clue.text: One hundred filled in hospital survey

indicators.note: something filled in goes into a space, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
san is short for sanatorium, a hospital

explanation.surface: A hundred people completed a questionnaire about a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or examine something quickly, a verb synonym of survey.

clue.text: Language examination, oral

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a check is an examination

explanation.surface: A spoken language test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral' looks like part of the exam's name, but it signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Czech is the Slavic tongue spoken in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Boss converted a loft on one residence

indicators.note: a converted loft has been rebuilt into something else, so its letters are rearranged
placed on means coming after in an across entry, so the rearranged letters follow the numeral

blocks.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
I is the Roman numeral one
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An employer turned an attic into a home for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer, but it is the ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a small one-room apartment, a kind of home or dwelling.

clue.text: Food processor taking seconds off when serving up cereal dish

indicators.note: in a down entry serving something up raises it, so it reads bottom to top
taking something off removes it from the word

blocks.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and fruit
s is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: A kitchen blender being used to make breakfast without second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' looks like a kitchen appliance, but it is a part of the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the last section of the small intestine, where digested food is absorbed.

clue.text: Low-grade criminal cursing in court

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the next one

blocks.note: a con is a convict
drat is a mild curse
a see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the papal court

explanation.surface: A petty crook swearing in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-grade criminal' reads as one phrase, but the adjective is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-rate is of inferior quality, so it is low-grade.

clue.text: Agreed on heading to racecourse here?

definitions.text: Agreed on heading to racecourse here?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its top, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: ay is a form of aye, yes
the first letter of racecourse

explanation.surface: A group settled on a racecourse to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: AYR is a Scottish town with a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr in Scotland has a racecourse, home of the Scottish Grand National, so racegoers might agree on it.

clue.text: Bird overhead hides

indicators.note: what a word hides is tucked inside it, so the answer lies within the letters

blocks.note: found inside the word

explanation.surface: A bird flying above takes cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Premises used in distributing sheet music, centrally

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle of the word, so only its central letter is kept
distributing things spreads them about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of music

explanation.surface: A building used for handing out printed scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premises' looks like a building, but it means propositions in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Theses are propositions put forward to be argued, so they work as the premises of a case.

clue.text: From afar, accommodation’s seen in Surrey, half-hidden

indicators.note: with half of it hidden, only the other half of the word shows
something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a motel is roadside accommodation
an English county south of London

explanation.surface: A distant view of lodgings in Surrey, partly screened.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for is. Surrey loses its first half, leaving REY to surround MOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Remotely means at a distance, so doing something remotely is doing it from far away.
